The second preview of CoSky 8.0. There is still **no compatibility promise**: the API, the wire format and the Redis keys may change before the beta, and nothing here is ready for real traffic. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

This one comes from trying what `8.0.0-alpha.1` had only simulated: a real OIDC provider, a real Kubernetes cluster, and the 20,000 connections of the design.

## Breaking

- **An Instance stays in its service.** A write that changes the `service` of an existing Instance now fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: delete it, then create it again. Those watching the old service used to keep seeing it for up to about 36 minutes. The default instance name holds the service, so this only comes up with a name of your own.

## Fixed

- **The server starts while the OIDC provider is away.** It used to exit, so an outage of the system people sign in with stopped replicas from starting. Applications carry on with their own tokens, and an ID token gets `UNAVAILABLE` until the provider is back.
- **The Dashboard renews its ID token.** People used to be signed out when it expired, which is 6 minutes on a default Keycloak, and lost what they were editing. It needs a provider that gives refresh tokens.
- **Signing out ends the session at the provider,** so the next sign-in asks for a password.
- **Large Configs no longer exhaust a replica's heap.** The Watch window is limited in bytes as well as in events, with `cosky.watch.window-bytes`, 64 MB per namespace by default.
- **A rolling update no longer resets connections.** The manifests wait 5 seconds in `preStop`, while the Service stops sending a stopping pod connections.
- **A clean shutdown no longer logs `Could not deregister`.**
- **Someone with no role is told so,** and sees the `sub` and groups to pass on to an administrator, rather than every page failing to load. People also appear by name rather than by an opaque id.

## Tried for real

- **OIDC:** Keycloak 26, as [Security](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/security#keycloak) describes. Other providers follow the same standard, but none has been tried.
- **Kubernetes:** k3s 1.31, with rolling updates, killed pods and Redis losing its data. CI now deploys every image on a real cluster.
- **Scale:** 20,000 connections and 100,000 watches all succeeded, in 7 seconds, in a Linux container. The earlier limit of about 15,000 was the load generator running out of ports on macOS. [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) has the figures.

## Known limits

To be settled before the beta:

- **Redis memory:** the Redis log is still limited in events only, so often-written large Configs can take `cosky.watch.window` times their size. [Sizing](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment#sizing) has the figures.
- **Propagation at 20,000 connections** is only borderline, when every write goes to every connection: a p99 of 171 to 525 ms in 6 runs of 7, against a target of 500 ms. The other run reached 5.8 seconds, and we do not know why.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **Not yet tried:** `kubectl drain` with several nodes, a real network between the parts, or Redis Cluster at this scale.
